text:
maria: Quick heads-up — I ran a micro-experiment on paged-attention OOM spikes. Added a "slot-balancer" that smooths workspace reserve over short windows (config: reserve_smooth_ms=500). Results attached below.
chen: Nice — what's the hypothesis? smoothing prevents big reserve jumps during mixed-length bursts?
alex: Did you change kernel routing/prefersmall? That often interacts.
maria: Exactly. Hypothesis: bursts of long sequences plus many small batches cause sudden workspace growth, triggering immediate compaction + kernel fallback. Smoothing staggers reserve changes so compaction gets fewer hard triggers. Also added a slot steal policy to prefer reusing cold blocks before allocating new big blocks.
maria: Quick numbers from 1h stress baseline vs smooth:
  - P99 latency (tokens/ms): baseline 12.4 -> smooth 12.7 (+2.4%)
  - OOM events / hour: baseline 8 -> smooth 1
  - KV cache hit rate: baseline 0.79 -> smooth 0.86
  - Compaction CPU time: baseline 4.2% -> smooth 7.9%
  - Small-kernel fallbacks during peak: baseline 3.1% -> smooth 5.6%
chen: So less OOM but higher compaction overhead and slightly more small kernel fallbacks. tradeoffs look reasonable for production, maybe tune smooth_ms.
sam: Did you try shorter windows? 500ms might be heavy on compaction frequency.
maria: Yes ran 250ms and 125ms quick runs:
  - 250ms: OOMs 2/hr, compaction 5.6%, P99 +1.2%
  - 125ms: OOMs 5/hr, compaction 4.8%, P99 +0.6%
  - baseline (0): OOMs 8/hr, compaction 4.2%, P99 +0.0%
alex: Interesting. 250ms looks like a good middle ground. Any change to block reuse policy?
maria: Enabled "cold-first-reuse" where blocks below reuse_threshold=0.15 get reclaimed for hot allocations. That reduced fragmentation but increased short-term compaction churn.
chen: Any kernel-routing policy changes? small-kernel fallback increase implies routing chose smaller kernels more. Is that from reserve smoothing delaying a big allocation and forcing smaller-kernel path?
maria: Precisely — when smoothing keeps reserved workspace lower, the kernel selector sometimes opts for the lower-memory kernel to stay under the (current) reserve. That keeps latency a bit higher on tails.
sam: Could we decouple kernel decision from transient reserve by adding an affordance flag: allow_kernel_affinity_override for X ms after smoothing event?
maria: Proposal: when smoothing triggers a reserve change, set kernel_affinity_grace_ms=200 so the prior kernel is more likely to be retained for that short time. Quick bench: with 250ms smoothing + 200ms affinity_grace:
  - P99: baseline +0.9%
  - OOMs: 1/hr
  - Compaction CPU: 6.1%
  - Small-kernel fallbacks: 2.8%
alex: That looks promising. Means we get OOM reduction with almost baseline P99. Can we produce a flamegraph or allocation timeline for the worst spike?
maria: Pushed a trace to the perf bucket: link: https://perf.redwood/internal/traces/2112346789-smoothed-slotbal. Highlights: repeated small allocs at t+14s, compaction at t+16s, reserve increase at t+16.2s.
chen: Any KV cache policy changes? smoother reserve increasing hit rate seems interesting.
maria: Two changes: 1) Keep KV cache prefetch window slightly larger when reserve smoothing enabled (prefetch_margin=128 tokens), 2) use eviction score that penalizes recently-demoted blocks less to favor reuse. Combined improved hit rate.
sam: Concern: compaction CPU up to ~6% might impact co-located workloads on dedicated nodes. For Dedicated we probably want 250ms only for bursty tiers, not steady throughput.
maria: Agreed. Plan: default off for Dedicated, enable as opt-in policy on hosted tier with safe defaults (reserve_smooth_ms=250, kernel_affinity_grace_ms=200, cold_first_reuse=on).
alex: Are there config knobs visible in the Console so SRE can toggle?
maria: I'll add route-level flags: "workspace.smoothing_ms", "workspace.affinity_grace_ms", "block.reuse_policy". Will add a quick Console toggle + audit log.
deploy-bot: deploy finished: canary 5% -> 100% :rocket:
maria: Action items:
  - maria: open PR with smoothing + affinity toggle and unit tests (WIP).
  - chen: run node-level cpu-impact test on Dedicated images (2h).
  - alex: add perf trace correlation to rollouts dashboard.
  - sam: prepare rollout doc for support + SLO notes.
chen: I'll run Dedicated test tonight and post numbers. :eyes:
maria: thanks — I'll cut a canary with 250ms+200ms in staging tomorrow morning.
sam: SGTM.
